title: Permitted Accounting Period
text:
Tax Administration Jamaica 

Practice Note 

Approval for the use of a 
Permitted Accounting  
Period 

This  Practice  Note  is  intended  only  as  a  general  guide  and  must  be  read  in 
conjunction with the relevant legislation. It contains the Authority’s interpretation 
of  the  law  as  it  stood  at  the  date  of  this  publication  along  with  any  associated 
practices, procedures and instructions. 

Under Section 12 (2) of the Tax Administration Jamaica Act, 2013 a Practice Note is 
binding  on  the  Commissioner  General  and  all  officers  of  the  Authority until  it  is 
revoked. However, taxpayers are reminded that the publication of a Practice Note 
does not affect their right of objection and appeal or their right of access to the 
Revenue Court on points concerning their own liability to Income Tax. 

Comments  and  suggestions  for  the  improvement  of  issued  Practice  Notes  and 
suggestions for future Practice Notes are always welcome. 

Ainsley Powell 
Commissioner General 
September 1, 2021

This Practice Note provides guidance with respect to the application in accordance with Section 6 
of the Income Tax Act of Jamaica for approval for a Permitted Accounting Period to end on some 
date other than December 31st.   

The examples in this Practice Note are strictly for purposes of illustrating the issues and concerns 
identified by Tax Administration Jamaica in making decisions on such approvals. 

All references herein are to the Income Tax Act unless otherwise indicated. 

This Practice Note supersedes previous publication dated July 1, 2019.

I. Glossary of Terms and Abbreviations 

The following list defines various terms used in this Practice Note. 

Accounting Period 

Basis Period 

An accounting period, in bookkeeping, is the period with reference to which 
accounting books of any entity are prepared. It is the period for which books 
are balanced and the financial statements are prepared. Generally, the 
accounting period consists of 12 months. 

“Basis Period” is the accounting period in a particular Year of Assessment for 
which a taxpayer is required to compute his or its taxable profit for Income 
Tax purposes and tax liability. 

It is usually the accounting period that coincides with the Year of Assessment 
but it can also be a Permitted Accounting Period. 

Body corporate 

A person, association, or group of persons legally incorporated 

Chargeable Income  

Section 2 of the Income Tax Act - "chargeable income" means the aggregate 
amount of income of any person from all sources remaining after allowing the 
appropriate deductions and exemptions under this Act. 

Default period 

Emoluments 

The default period for tax purposes is the "year of assessment", i.e. the period 
of twelve months commencing on the 1st day of January in each year. 

Includes, in relation to any office or employment of profit, items as defined in 
Section 2 of the ITA.  

First Effective Year 

This is the first year of the newly requested accounting period. It is the first 
taxable year for which a change in annual accounting period is effective.  

Financial Year 

A financial year is a period of twelve months, used by business, and other 
organizations in order to calculate their budgets, profits, and losses. It is any 
annual period at the end of which a firm's accounts are closed and financial 
reports are prepared. Section 2 of the CA stipulates that, in relation to a body 
corporate, this is the period in respect of which any profit and loss account of 
the body corporate, laid before it in general meeting is made up, whether 
that period is a year or not. 

Gains or profits of 
any trade, 
profession or 
business 

Any compensation, payments or benefits due to or received by any person in 
the furtherance of a trade, business or profession. Section 2 of the Income 
Tax Act defines "trade" to include every trade, manufacture, adventure or 
concern in the nature of trade.  The term “Profession has not been defined in 

1 

                                                                                                
 
 
 
 UPN-PAP 02-2021                                                                                            

the Act but its literal meaning as defined by many scholars and accountancy 
bodies identifies it as a vocation, or a job requiring some thought, skill and 
special knowledge like that of accountant, lawyer, doctor, engineer, architect 
etc. So profession refers to those activities where the livelihood is earned by 
the persons through their intellectual or manual skill. Section 5 of the Income 
Tax Act of Jamaica gives more meaning to “profits or gains” which are 
chargeable to income tax. 

For the purposes of the Practice Note a “newly registered business” is a 
person who has not previously filed an income tax return for any year of 
assessment and who will be filing the first return using a date other than the 
31st day of December. 

Permitted accounting period, in relation to any person, means the accounting 
period, other than a 12-month period ending December 31st, in respect of 
which the gains or profits of any trade, profession or business carried on or 
exercised by that person are permitted or required to be computed pursuant 
to Sections 6 (2), 6 (3), 5, or 6 (4) of the ITA. 

"Permitted accounting terminal date", in relation to any permitted accounting 
period, means the ending date of the period. 

As stated in Section 2 of the ITA "person" means any individual and also any 
body of persons. 

Newly registered 
business 

Permitted 
Accounting Period 

Permitted 
Accounting Terminal 
date 

Person 

Required Submission 
Time 

A period of not less than 60 working days prior to the start date of the new 
proposed accounting period for which an application for a permitted 
accounting period is being made. 

Specified Period 

Statutory income 

Taxpayer 

A period of five years within which a person to whom approval was granted 
for a permitted accounting period is not allowed to make a new application 
(with exceptions).   

Subject to section 6 of the ITA, the aggregate amount of income of any 
person from all sources remaining after allowing the appropriate deductions 
and exemptions… 

Section 2 of The Revenue Administration (Amendment) Act, 2013 defines a 
“taxpayer” to include a person who 
(a) Is liable to pay tax pursuant to a revenue law of Jamaica whether or not –  

(i)  The person is resident of Jamaica; 
(i)  The tax liability is in question; or 
(ii)  In the event, any payment is waived or remitted or no amount is 

found to be payable; 

(b) Is of relevance to a treaty partner in respect of an international tax 

2 

                                                                                                
 
 
 UPN-PAP 02-2021                                                                                            

agreement. 

Tax Year  

The year for which an income tax return is being filed.  It is usually a particular 
period of twelve months beginning on January 1st and ending on December 
31st.

 UPN-PAP 02-2021                                                                                            

III. Purpose 

1.  The purpose of this document is to provide guidance to the public in general on the 

interpretation of the provisions of Sections 6 (2), 6(3), & 6(4) of the Income Tax Act of 
Jamaica and more specifically, guidance on the application and approval for a permitted 
accounting period, i.e., an accounting date terminating on a date other than 31st day of 
December.  

2.  This PN sets out the factors to be taken into consideration when making a request to the 
CG to allow an alternative accounting period, other than one ending December 31st. 

3.  This PN seeks to ensure that the decision on whether to allow an entity to adopt a 

permitted accounting period involves balancing the interests of that entity with that of 
the Revenue thereby ensuring an efficiently administered income tax system.  

IV. Objectives 

This Practice Note is: 

4.  To provide guidance to persons affected by the law and to the officers of TAJ.  This is in 
accordance with Section 12 of the Tax Administration Jamaica Act, 2013 which states 
that the CG may issue Practice Notes setting out the interpretation and procedures for 
the application of the Law. 

5.  To promote and achieve consistency in the administration of the Laws relating to 
domestic tax. It is also to be used to streamline the processing of applications for 
approval of a permitted accounting period to improve efficiency and service to 
taxpayers. 

6.  To provide taxpayers with a degree of certainty regarding specific policies, guidelines 

and procedures on the application and approval for a change of accounting year end to 
some date other than 31st day of December, i.e., a permitted accounting period.  

7.  To provide taxpayers with a degree of certainty regarding specific policies, guidelines 

and procedures in instances where approval was granted by the CG: 

(a)  For a change in accounting year to some date other than 31st day of December 

and the taxpayer makes a subsequent request for another change.  

4 

                                                                                                
 
 
 
 
 
 UPN-PAP 02-2021                                                                                            

(b) For a change in accounting year to some date other than 31st day of December 
and the taxpayer has now made a subsequent request to revert to the default 
year ending 31st day of December.  

8.  To provide taxpayers with a degree of certainty regarding specific policies, guidelines 

and procedures in instances where no approval was granted by the CG: 

(a)  For a change in accounting year to some date other than 31st day of December. 

(b) For a change in accounting year to some date other than 31st day of December 
and the taxpayer has now made a subsequent request to revert to the default 
year ending 31st day of December.  

V. Scope & Background  

9.  In administering the law relating to a permitted accounting period, this Practice Note 

sets out the interpretation and administrative rules of the CG in respect to Section 6 of 
the ITA governing the change in accounting period to a permitted accounting period. It 
also provides TAJ’s position with respect to the submission of an application for 
approval of the change.  

10. The requirement for the approval of any planned change in an entity’s accounting 

period for Income Tax purposes has long been in existence and is in accordance with the 
law. However, there were no recommended rules and guidelines for instructing the 
taxpayer on how to secure this approval for a permitted accounting period. 

11. Where a date other than the default period is being used and the CG is not aware of 

this, the taxpayer’s income tax account on TAJ’s database will not reflect this change. As 
such, the CG intends to ensure that the RAIS is properly configured to evaluate the 
expectations of each taxpayer who is required to file returns.  

12. Therefore, if an existing taxpayer wishes to change their accounting period from the 
default period to any other 12-month period or a new taxpayer wishes to adopt an 
accounting period other than the default period, the net income shall, with the approval 
of the CG, be computed on the basis of such new proposed accounting period. 

13. In considering a request to change to a permitted accounting period, the CG will look at 
relevant matters, consistent with the statutory responsibilities under Section 6 of the 
ITA so as to maintain the integrity of the tax system. 

5 

                                                                                                
 
 
 
 UPN-PAP 02-2021                                                                                            

VI. Need for a policy guideline 

14. There was no fixed period within which to make the request to secure the approval of 
the CG. The ITA is silent on a required timeframe within which to make a request for 
securing the CG’s approval for a permitted accounting period. 

15. A permitted accounting period affects the deadlines/due dates for paying income tax 

and filing of an Income Tax Return. 

16. Section 6 (2) of the ITA establishes that a person can make a request for permission for 
their accounting year to end on a date other than the 31st day of December.  However, 
there is no provision for instances where an individual has multiple sources of income, 
inclusive of emoluments. 

17. There is no clear instruction advising the taxpayer how to separate the income when a 

new business files its first return and is required to file two separate returns. 

18. Stakeholders are uncertain about their filing obligations as it relates to the ‘Date of 

Incorporation’ & ‘Date of Trading’ and the effects for persons requesting a permitted 
accounting period. This is on the premise that both dates may not always be the same. 

19. Section 6, despite giving the instruction to separate into two returns, would not have 

contemplated the late penalty charges that would now be applicable under Section 71B. 
At the time Section 6 was written into law a late filing penalty provision was not yet 
brought into law. 

VII. Statutory requirements for a permitted accounting period 

20. Sections 6(2), 6(3) & 6(4) of the ITA generally provides that a taxpayer who wishes to 
change its accounting period and use a permitted accounting period must obtain the 
approval of the CG  

21.  Section 6 (2) provides that, in conjunction with subsection (1), where the CG is satisfied 
that any person usually makes up the accounts of his trade, profession or business to 
some date other than the 31st day of December he may permit the gains or profits of 
that trade, profession or business to be computed upon the income for the period of 
twelve months terminating on that date in the year of assessment to which the 
accounts of that trade, profession or business are usually made up.  

6 

                                                                                                
 
 
 
 
 UPN-PAP 02-2021                                                                                            

22.  Section 6 (3) of the ITA provides that where a person commencing to carry on a trade, 
profession or business satisfies the CG that he/she intends to make up the accounts to 
a date other than the 31st day of December, the CG may grant permission under 
subsection (2). 

23.  Where permission is granted as per Section 6 (2) and under circumstances where 

(a)  the first accounts of the trade, profession or business have not yet been drawn 

up; and  

(b) the first accounts of a trade, profession or business covers a period which 

exceeds twelve months,  

the income of the period shall be treated for this purpose as being apportioned at an 
even rate between the twelve months terminating on the date to which the accounts 
are made up and the remainder of the period.   

24. Under Section 6 (4) of the ITA where a person departs from his permitted accounting 

terminal date, i.e.  his ending date.  

(a)  The new permitted accounting period will be determined by the CG identifying:  

(i)  The Y/A in which the departure occurs and 
(ii)  The Y/A immediately following the departure period 

(b) The permitted accounting period determined by the CG for the Y/A in which the 

departure occurred may include any interval between the end of the old 
accounting period and the commencement date of the new permitted 
accounting period. 

(c)  The terminal date of the new permitted accounting period as determined by the 
CG will be regarded as the permitted accounting terminal date of this person 
until another permitted accounting period has been requested in accordance 
with the provisions of the legislation and the guidelines of this PN. 

25. After a determination of the taxpayer’s permitted accounting period has been made by 
the CG in accordance with section 6 (4), if the taxpayer subsequently chooses to change 
his permitted accounting period, the taxpayer must first seek approval from the CG. Any 
further applications for change will be assessed in accordance with the criteria set out in 
section 6(2) & (3) of the Income Tax Act. 

7 

                                                                                                
 
 
 
 
 
 UPN-PAP 02-2021                                                                                            

VIII. Commissioner’s Powers 

26. Under PART VID, Section 17O of the Revenue Administration (Amendment) Act, 2013 

the CG  

(i)   “May establish an electronic communication system (in this section referred to as 

the "system”) including provision for any or all of the following operations- 

(a)  filing of electronic documents with the Commissioner General;  
(b) service or issue of electronic documents by the Commissioner 
(c)  ………………………….. 

(ii)  For the purposes of subsection (1), the Commissioner General may make rules 

providing for any or all of the following 

(a)  ……………………………… 
(b) the type of documents that may be sent through the system including the 

format and manner of sending them, ………………………… 

(c)  the format for, and the content of, information that is to be included in 

documents sent through the system; 

(d) ……………………………………….. 
(f)  the determination of when a document that is filed through use of the 

system is received by the Commissioner General; 

(g)  …………………. 
(h) any other matter for the better administration or operation of the system. 

(iii) An electronic document that is communicated by means of the system is deemed to 
have been received by the person to whom it is communicated, unless the contrary 
is shown.” 

27. Section 18A of the Revenue Administration (Amendment) Act, 2013 states that 

“Without limiting the powers of the Minister under Section 19, the Commissioner 
General may, by order published in the Gazette prescribe forms of returns and other 
forms that the Commissioner General considers to be necessary for the various purposes 
of this Act, whether for general use or use in any particular case or for the use of any 
particular person or group of persons” 

8 

                                                                                                
 
 
 
 
 
 
 UPN-PAP 02-2021                                                                                            

28. Section 71B of the ITA - Penalty for late filing of return- states that “The Commissioner 
General may waive or reduce a penalty that is incurred under subsection (1) if the 
Commissioner General is satisfied that there are circumstances that justify doing so.” 

IX. Taxpayers’ Obligations 

29. The taxpayer must submit a request for the use of a permitted accounting period using 

the eservices account. Step-by-step instructions can be found on TAJ’s website 
https://www.jamaicatax.gov.jm/web/guest/how-to.. “How-to Request Permitted 
Accounting Period Approval via eServices” (Exhibit 1) 

30. For income tax purposes, any taxpayer who proposes to change his accounting year end 
shall, before using the new period, comply with the provisions of the ITA relating to a 
permitted accounting period by securing the approval of the CG to change the 
accounting year end on some date other than the 31st day of December.  

31. For newly registered businesses the CG has used his discretionary powers to allow new 
registrants to identify and adopt the period so identified as its permitted accounting 
period when they file their first return. Therefore, they will be required to file their first 
Income Tax Return for that newly registered business with a year-end other that 31st 
day of December on or before the due date ascribed to that accounting year end, 

32. Further to paragraph 31, where the newly registered businesses will be allowed to 

identify and adopt an accounting year end other than 31st day of December, and the 
first accounts of a trade, profession or business (i.e. first accounting period upon 
commencement of trading) covers a period which exceeds twelve months they will be 
required to apportion their income at an even rate between the twelve months 
terminating on the date to which the accounts are made up and the remainder of the 
period.  

33. The taxpayer will be required to file two separate returns. Both returns must be aligned 
to the permitted accounting period being requested.  The CG has instructed that the 
filing sequence for the returns will be the shorter period then the 12 month-period 
while applying the relevant credits and capital allowances associated with each Y/A.  

9 

                                                                                                
 
 
 
 
 
 UPN-PAP 02-2021                                                                                            

X. Who will be allowed a permitted accounting period? 

34. Section 6(2) of the ITA provides for any person to request an approval for a permitted 

accounting period. 

35. Section 2 of the ITA defines “person” as any individual and also as any body of persons. 
"Body of persons" means any body politic, corporate or collegiate, and any company, 
fraternity, fellowship and society of persons, whether corporate or not corporate. 

36. Bodies corporate, regardless of business type may be permitted to change their 

accounting period to end on some date other than December 31st. Generally, individuals 
must adopt the calendar year as their default period; however, Section 6 of the ITA does 
not preclude them from requesting a change.  

37. For individuals, approval to use an accounting period ending with a date other than 

December 31st must include the full emoluments earned for the calendar year in which 
the permitted accounting period ends. The CG will not allow apportionment of 
emoluments when accounting for the profits and gains. In determining the liability, the 
income tax threshold relevant to that Y/A must be used. Take note that emoluments 
normally accrue on a monthly basis and must be accounted for in a Y/A.  (see 
Illustration 1)  

XI. Reasons for requesting a permitted accounting period 

38. Taxpayers will require a permitted accounting period based on sound business reasons. 
The CG’s view is that the following non-exhaustive list of reasons could constitute 
"sound business reasons": 

(i) A person may change accounting year in order to consolidate the filings of their 

Income Tax return if they are operating in a group environment or have to make 
international filings; 

(ii) A person changes its accounting period to end on the same date as that of its 

parent or associated company; 

(iii) A person changes its accounting period to ease financial reporting requirements 

under various legislations and to various reporting entities; 

(iv) A person may wish to adopt a change to its accounting period when they can 

10 

                                                                                                
 
 
 
 
 UPN-PAP 02-2021                                                                                            

demonstrate that the nature of their business makes a December 31st year end 
impractical; or their circumstances have changed significantly and they should be 
permitted to change to some date other than December 31st.  

(v) To avoid busy trading periods. Entities might wish to avoid having to prepare 

accounts or conduct stock takes during their busy periods; 

(vi)  A person may wish to adopt a permitted accounting period for business entities 
with a close working relationship, where they share a common business and/or 
management accounting system or central administration structure and one of 
those entities already has a permitted accounting period. This category includes 
joint ventures that want to adopt an accounting period common with that of its 
partner; 

(vii) Persons who were granted a permitted accounting period or who had, without 
prior approval, used a period other than the default period, may subsequently 
want to revert to the default filing period. 

However, neither the personal convenience of the taxpayer, nor the saving or deferment of 
income taxes will be considered a "sound business reason".  

XII. Procedures for granting approval for a permitted 

accounting period 

39. The CG, has exercised his powers under Sections 17O & 18A of the Revenue 

Administration (Amendment) Act, 2013, and has instructed that, effective September 
13, 2021 it will be mandatory that the request for a permitted accounting period be 
made on-line via TAJ’s Tax Portal using the prescribed form designed for that purpose. 

40. If the tax returns are already overdue at the date of application, the taxpayer will not be 

approved for the use of a permitted accounting period.  

41. When agreeing to a change to an accounting period, the CG will only agree to a 

permitted accounting period with a year-end that is the last calendar day of a month. No 
other permitted accounting period terminal date will be accommodated. 

42. A permitted accounting period will remain in effect until the entity applies for, and is 

granted permission to adopt another permitted accounting period.  

11 

                                                                                                
 
 
 
 
 UPN-PAP 02-2021                                                                                            

43. Where a newly registered business was granted approval to use a permitted accounting 

through the first annual return filed, which was his de facto application granting 
permission to use such date, any change for the use some other must be applied for 
using a PAP01 application form. This taxpayer will not be allowed to file an amended 
return to effect a change to some other date. 

44. Where permission was previously granted for an entity to use an accounting period 

ending on some date other than December 31st and the entity now wishes to revert to a 
period ending December 31st it will be required to submit a PAP01 application form 
seeking permission to do so. 

45. Where a decision was taken not to allow a permitted accounting period, the CG will 

provide the taxpayer with a full explanation of the reasons. While there are no objection 
rights against a decision not to allow a permitted accounting period, the taxpayer may 
seek to have the CG review his decision and provide the CG with reasons why it is felt 
that the decision so made was incorrect. 

XIII. When to file an application for a permitted accounting 

period 

46. The request for approval for a permitted accounting period must be done within the 

required submission time. The request must be submitted not less than 60 working days 
before the beginning of the proposed new accounting period. 

(a)  A taxpayer that is already registered to file income tax returns must submit such 

an application to TAJ no less than 60 working days before the start of the 
proposed new accounting period. However, TAJ recommends that the 
application be submitted as early as possible to provide TAJ with adequate time 
to respond to the request prior to the proposed new accounting period and the 
due date of the taxpayer’s return for the first effective year. 

(b) Any taxpayer whose application is submitted less than 60 working days before 

the start of the proposed new accounting period may have their request denied. 
The taxpayer may be asked to continue using the existing accounting period and 
make a resubmission for a permitted accounting period in keeping with the 
required time frame given in this PN.  

12 

                                                                                                
 
 
 
 UPN-PAP 02-2021                                                                                            

(c)  However, the CG may consider an application that has been filed after the 

required submission time. If special circumstances exist, a taxpayer may also 
request an extension of time to submit their application giving reasonable cause 
for such delay. (see paragraphs 47- 48).  

Exception to the general submission rule, as indicated in paragraph 46, will be granted 
to a newly registered business whose first set of accounts exceed 12 months. 
Submission of their first set of accounts will be their default application for approval to 
use a permitted accounting period. Invariably, submission of the two returns will not 
meet the specified submission period. 

XIV. Applications submitted after the specified time  

47. Any application submitted less than 60 working days before the start of the proposed 
new accounting period may be considered as a timely submission if the taxpayer 
establishes that he/she acted reasonably and in good faith, giving a reasonable cause for 
the delay in submitting the application and that granting approval will not prejudice the 
interest of the Revenue.  

48. The CG may consider unusual and compelling circumstances or any such occurrence 

which prevents a taxpayer from applying for a permitted accounting period within the 
specified time. These can include, but not limited to: 

-  Serious illness or accident; and serious emotional or mental distress, such as 

death in the immediate family; 

-  Natural disasters, such as a flood, fire, hurricane, earthquake; 
-  Civil disturbances or disruptions in services, such as a riot, incursion; 

49. If a taxpayer’s circumstances do not fall within the situations described above but the 

CG is satisfied with the explanation the taxpayer provides, the CG may consider such an 
application to be timely. 

Notwithstanding, no extension will be given that will cause a return to be filed late. 

13 

                                                                                                
 
 
 
 
 
 UPN-PAP 02-2021                                                                                            

XV. Adoption of a permitted accounting period by new 

registrant 

50. Given the powers under Section 6 (2) & (3) of the ITA the CG will permit a newly 

registered business, to adopt a permitted accounting period ending on a date other than 
31st day of December by filing its first Income Tax Return using that period, which then 
becomes its default application for permission. After a newly registered business has 
adopted an accounting year, it must continue to use that accounting year when 
computing its taxable income.   

51. A permitted accounting period will remain in effect until the taxpayer applies for, and is 

granted permission to adopt another permitted accounting period.  

XVI. Changing a permitted accounting period to another 

permitted accounting period 

52. Section 6 (4)(a) states that where a taxpayer has departed from its permitted accounting 
terminal date the CG may require the taxpayer to use as the relevant accounting period 
for that Y/A in which the departure occurred, and the following year, such periods as the 
CG may determine. The period determined by the CG, in relation to the departure, may 
include any interval between the permitted accounting date of the old accounting period 
and the commencement of the new accounting period. (see Illustration 2) 

53. Change is to a date later in the year than the original PAP: When there is a change in 
permitted accounting period there will be profits of a basis period of more or less than 
twenty-four (24) months to be assessed in two years of assessment. If the change is to a 
date later in the year than the original permitted accounting date, there will be more 
than 24 months’ profits to be assessed in the Y/A in which the departure took place and 
the next succeeding year. The law provides that the excess may be included in the year 
in which the departure took place. The year in which the departure took place is the Y/A 
in which falls the date to which an account of the old permitted accounting period 
should have been made up to or the date to which an account on the new permitted 
accounting date is made up, whichever is earlier. (See Illustration 3 & 4) 

54. Change is to a date earlier than the original PAP: Where the change is to a date earlier 
than the original permitted accounting date then there will be less than 24 months’ 

14 

                                                                                                
 
 
 
 
 UPN-PAP 02-2021                                                                                            

profits to be assessed in the Y/A in which the departure took place and the next 
succeeding year. The law provides that the permitted accounting period for the year in 
which the departure took place and the next succeeding year shall be such period as the 
CG may determine.  

55. Normally such determination will be that the permitted accounting period for the year 
in which the departure took place will be the period between the permitted accounting 
terminal date of the old permitted accounting period and the commencement of the 
new permitted accounting period. This means the departure year is for a period of less 
than 12 months and that the accounting period for the next succeeding year will be 12 
months ending on the new permitted accounting date. (See Illustration 5)  

56. Where a taxpayer had already filed a first return with a PAP then that taxpayer will have 
no recourse but to make an application for a change in PAP using the PAP01 application 
form. The first return submitted with an accounting year ending with a date other than 
December 31st would have been accepted as the de facto application for a PAP at that 
time of filing. Any subsequent changes can only be accommodated through an 
application using the PAP01 form. 

XVII. How often can a person apply? 

57. A person will generally not be allowed to apply for more than one change within a 

specified period, with exceptions. (see paragraph 59). The specified period is considered 
to be a period of five years within which a person to whom approval was granted for a 
permitted accounting period is not allowed to make a new application.  

58. However, a request for permitted accounting period can be made more than once 

within the specified period but the taxpayer is obligated to ensure that the provisions as 
laid out in Section 6 of the ITA regarding the approval is adhered to. 

59. In the CG’s assessment of the application for another change within a specified period 
the CG will look at whether or not there are extenuating circumstances requiring the 
change, such as: 

-  Aligning the accounting period with that of a subsidiary or its parent company; 
-  Where the companies are operating in a group environment; 
-  Where the business is in liquidation. 

15 

                                                                                                
 
 
 
 
 UPN-PAP 02-2021                                                                                            

Take note, it is not possible to set out all the circumstances in which an approval may or 
may not be granted therefore each case will be considered on its merits, taking into 
account all the relevant facts. 

60. Where a taxpayer has made more than one request for change in permitted accounting 
period within the specified period and there is evidence of misuse of the facility, the CG 
reserves the right to deny approval of the latest application.  

61. Where a subsequent application is submitted for a change to another permitted 

accounting period, the taxpayer must ensure that the following information is attached 
to his new application: 

Permitted accounting period that was approved but not implemented by the 
taxpayer 

Where an entity failed to implement the period approved by the CG an explanation 
must be furnished stating why the permitted accounting period was not used. TAJ 
will consider the explanation in determining whether the subsequent request for a 
change in the accounting period should be granted. 

62. The CG’s approval for a permitted accounting period will be provided in a letter from 

the office of the Technical Specialist Unit of TAJ. The letter will be generated within RAIS 
once the mandatory online application takes effect on September 13, 2021.  

XVIII. Taxpayer required to file returns in accordance with 

Sections 67, 69(2), 71A of the ITA 

63. Section 67 states that “…… every person liable to pay income tax in respect of any year 

of assessment shall deliver, or cause to be delivered by his agent, to the Commissioner of 
Inland Revenue, or to the Collector or Assistant Collector of Taxes for the parish in which 
he resides, a true and correct return of the whole of his income from every source 
whatsoever for that year of assessment and ….” 

64. Section 69 (2) states that “……shall make and deliver a return of the income of the 

partnership for any year of assessment, such income being ascertained in accordance 
with the provisions of this Act, ….” 

16 

                                                                                                
 
 
 
 
 
 UPN-PAP 02-2021                                                                                            

65. Section 71A of the ITA requires that  

“Notwithstanding any other provision of this Act, every person to whom this section 
applies shall, in respect of each year of assessment, file a return in such form, and 
containing such particulars, as may be prescribed, regardless of whether that person – 

(a) is liable to pay income tax in respect of that year of assessment; or 

(b) has income from any source for that year of assessment 

(2) This section applies to the following persons – 

(e) a body corporate that is incorporated, registered or constituted under any 
enactment; (f) a trust or other institution (whether incorporated or not) that is registered 
as a charitable organization under the Charities Act; and (g) any person (including an 
individual) who carries on, or has carried on, a trade, profession, vocation or business 
and who is prescribed for the purposes of this section by order of the Minister, subject to 
negative resolution of the House of Representatives.” 

66. Persons so instructed under these sections, especially section 71A, will be required to 

file their income tax return regardless of whether or not it is liable to pay income tax in 
respect of that year of assessment or has income from any source for that year of 
assessment. Where a partnership is requesting the use of a PAP the partners must 
conform to the requirements of Sections 69(2) & Section 71A. 

67. Newly registered business, falling under Sections 67, 69 (2) and 71A, who are using a 
permitted accounting period, and whose incorporation date and trading date differs 
may come into conflict with the requirements of these sections. 

68. For a newly registered business falling under these sections, and more specifically under 
Section 71A, where the incorporation date and the trading date differs there is always 
the likelihood that a conflict with this section will occur. The taxpayer requesting a PAP 
will be allowed to complete the first set of accounts and file this return which now 
becomes the de facto application for the PAP. However, the persons using a PAP, and 
who submits their first set of accounts for a period in excess of 12 months, will discover 
that the first of the two returns will be late. Invariably, the provision under this section 
of the law will not be fulfilled and additionally that first return will attract late filing 
penalty charges as imposed by Section 71B of the ITA and interest charges as per Section 
79 (2)(b).   

17 

                                                                                                
 
 
 UPN-PAP 02-2021                                                                                            

69. Where a person falls under Section 71A in a year of assessment and commenced trading 
activities in a subsequent year of assessment, in order to meet the requirements of 
Section 71A, the first return, and any outstanding return since coming under Section 
71A, must also be aligned to the PAP being requested. (i.e. both returns must conform 
to the PAP being requested) (Illustration 6).  

70. For a newly registered business falling within Section 71A, where the incorporation date 
and the trading date is the same, there should be no conflict with this section. The 
taxpayer requesting a PAP will be allowed to complete its first set of accounts and file its 
return which now becomes the de facto application for the PAP. (see Illustration 7)  

71. The CG, under his discretionary powers is willing to waive the late filing penalty charges 
which would be imposed under Section 71B and interest charges as per Section 79 (2)(b), 
provided the second of the two returns is submitted on or before the due date. Should 
the returns now being filed using a PAP be submitted late then none of the charges will be 
waived. 

XIX. Processing time to respond to application 

72. The approval for a permitted accounting period must be made by TAJ within 30 working 
days from the date of receipt of all the documents required to process the application.  

73. Where the CG has denied an application for a permitted accounting period, the taxpayer 
must be formally advised of the reason(s) for denial within 30 working days from the 
date of receipt of all the documents required to process the application. 

XX. How to treat an unauthorized permitted accounting 

period? 

74. Despite the strictness of the provisions in Section 6 of the ITA, the CG has taken the 

decision that any unauthorized change made by a taxpayer, to use some date other than 
December 31st, prior to the publication of this PN will be accepted as their permitted 
accounting period (see Illustration 8).   

18 

                                                                                                
 
 
 
 
 UPN-PAP 02-2021                                                                                            

75. Therefore, all unauthorized changes will be ratified by the CG and the taxpayer will be 

formally advised of this decision. (see Exhibit 2). However, for any unauthorized change 
which occurs after September 13, 2021 the CG will enforce the provisions of Section 6 of 
the ITA as well as the procedures laid out in paragraphs 39– 45 of this PN. 

76. Individuals with multiple sources of income inclusive of emoluments who have been 
using some date other than December 31st must now conform to the instructions   in 
paragraph 37.  

77. To the extent that an individual had apportioned his emoluments in keeping with the 

accounting period that was in use, that individual must now account for the remaining 
emoluments for that year of assessment on his next return. However, that individual will 
only be entitled to the unutilized PAYE credit, if any, from the prior calendar year, in 
addition to the PAYE credit from the emoluments earned in the next year of assessment. 
(see Illustration 9).   

XXI. Retroactive change in permitted accounting period 

78. Retroactive changes in a permitted accounting period for the personal convenience of 

the taxpayer is not permitted.  

79. No approval for a retroactive change in accounting period to a date other than 

December 31st will be approved wherein the change will prejudice the interest of the 
Revenue. 

80. The taxpayer’s accounting period can only be changed when the request is prompted 

solely on sound business reasons, as indicated in paragraph 38 above.  

81. Unless specifically authorized by the CG, a taxpayer may not make a retroactive change 
in an accounting period regardless of whether the change is to revert the taxpayer back 
to the default filing period. 

82. The CG will use his discretionary powers under Section 6 (3) to allow the newly 

registered business to make a PAP request. In such an instance it might appear to be 
retroactive where the taxpayer is required by law to file two returns when the first set 
of accounts exceeds 12 months. The annual return for the shorter filing period will 
invariably have a retroactive period since it must be aligned to the PAP requested in the 
de facto application/return. Under such circumstances the CG will accept the first return 
which will bear a retroactive PAP.

XXII. Capital Allowance Treatment 

83. Where a permitted accounting period results in a period greater than or less than 

twelve (12) months, the capital allowance to be claimed is dependent on whether the 
asset is in use at the end of the basis period. 

XXIII. What is the treatment for prior approval letters? 

84. Where a taxpayer previously received the necessary approval as outlined in Section 6 of 

the ITA, such approval will continue to be valid until the taxpayer makes another 
request to change to some other date. At that time, the procedures laid out in 
paragraphs 39– 45 of this PN and Section 6 (4) (b) of the ITA must be followed.

Illustration 6: Date of incorporation and trading date differs.  

Taxpayer 1 is body corporate incorporated under the Companies Act of Jamaica on May 1, 2018. 

They did not file a return from the date of incorporation on May 1, 2018. Taxpayer 1 was of the 
opinion that it was not necessary since no trading activities had begun until March 1, 2019 and 
also intends to use an accounting year ending June 30. Taxpayer 1 attempted to file its first 
return electronically starting from the commencement of trading with financial data covering a 
16-month accounting period but is advised that returns are needed from the period of 
incorporation, i.e. 2018. 

Section 71A of the ITA requires that Taxpayer 1 file its income tax return regardless of whether 
or not it is liable to pay income tax in respect of that year of assessment or has income from any 
source for that year of assessment. Where a person falls under Section 71A in a year of 
assessment and commenced trading activities in a subsequent year of assessment, in order to 
meet the requirements of Section 71A, the first return, and any outstanding return since coming 
under Section 71A, should be aligned to the permitted accounting period being requested. 

Therefore, since Taxpayer 1 is requesting a permitted accounting period it would be required to 
file its 2018 return from the date of incorporation, aligning it to the June 30 year-end proposed. 
The first set of accounts for a 16-month period as at commencement must be realigned to a 
June 30 which would cover the period of trading as well as the periods of non-trading. 
Therefore, Taxpayer 1 will need to adjust its first set of accounts at the commencement of trade 
to 24 months so that there is no gap in the accounting period on the returns being filed.
